purpose: Determine whether the FreeCAD Draft DWG-to-DXF handoff can qualify 3DSOLID ACIS/SAT geometry semantics.

sources.title: FreeCAD Draft DXF documentation
sources.finding: FreeCAD documents that 3D DXF solids are stored as ACIS/SAT blobs and cannot currently be read. The built-in C++ importer entity list does not include 3DSOLID, REGION, or BODY. DWG is converted to DXF and then passed to that importer.
sources.authority: Project documentation; current upstream page observed 2026-11-12

sources.title: FreeCAD issue 18454
sources.finding: FreeCAD maintainers state that ACIS solids in DXF are an unreadable proprietary blob in the current importer path.

sources.title: Installed FreeCAD 1.1.4 Draft importer
sources.finding: The post-processing layer wraps shapes delivered by the C++ importer but does not itself decode ACIS/SAT. This local source inspection is supplementary; it does not stand in for the documented C++ importer capability boundary.

routeConclusion: FreeCAD Draft importDWG -> dwg2dxf -> built-in importDXF is a 2D/ordinary-entity consumer route, not an ACIS 3DSOLID semantic oracle. The separate FreeCAD Part construction from SAT through the research InventorLoader parser is a native kernel check, but not a native DXF/DWG import check and shares OpenCASCADE with that parser.
planEffect: Keep FreeCAD 2D open/insert qualification in P8. Do not spend implementation time trying to qualify ACIS/SAT 3DSOLID by the built-in FreeCAD DXF importer. Continue P7 with its independent reader/kernel and source-native gates, and qualify 3D consumers whose documented import route consumes the selected ACIS carrier.
limitations: No FreeCAD DXF import was run for an ACIS-bearing file; the authoritative documentation and maintainer response already identify the importer boundary.
This does not qualify or disqualify FreeCAD Part's separate SAT construction route.
No DWG/DXF fixture was added, and no support claim is promoted.
